reasoning: Both models reviewed the same 5 files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, REUSE.toml, and two LICENSE files) and found no security issues. The PKGBUILD is a standard Rust build with pinned source tarball from GitHub and SHA-256 checksum verification. All build functions (prepare, build, check, package) use standard cargo commands with --locked/--frozen flags. No dangerous top-level code execution, no network requests beyond the declared source, no obfuscated code, and no execution of externally fetched scripts. The .SRCINFO matches the PKGBUILD metadata. LICENSE files are standard ISC license text. REUSE.toml is standard licensing metadata. The 'inconclusive' result from Report 1 was caused by a transient API error (HTTP 400) on the first LICENSE review attempt, not by any actual security concern—the second attempt succeeded and marked LICENSE as safe.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in Report 1 (qwen3-235b). The model encountered an HTTP 400 BadRequestError when first reviewing LICENSE, which caused the overall audit result to be marked 'inconclusive' even though the retry succeeded and marked the file safe. Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) completed without errors and correctly returned 'safe'. This is a tooling/reliability issue, not a substantive security disagreement.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen3-235b) experienced an API error (HTTP 400) on first LICENSE review, causing inconclusive result despite successful retry
learnings: When a file review fails due to transient API errors but succeeds on retry, the audit tool should not mark the overall result as 'inconclusive' if all files were eventually reviewed successfully
The audit tool should distinguish between 'file review failed and could not be retried' vs 'file review failed but retry succeeded' when computing final verdict

Duplicate file entries in review logs (LICENSE appearing twice) suggest the tool may be processing the same file multiple times or there are multiple license files—this should be clarified in reporting
